newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: French adventurer forced to cancel sea quest.
newsitem.headline: French adventurer forced to cancel sea quest.

text.p: A kidney complaint has forced French adventurer Guy Delage on Wednesday to postpone indefinitely his planned expedition to spend up to 90 days drifting under the Indian Ocean locked inside a steel capsule.
A statement from the project organisers said Delage, in Singapore for final tests of his Ocean Observer craft, was in hospital undergoing tests for suspected renal colic.

"The unexpected occurrence will cause a serious delay in the state of the oceanographic mission," the statement said. It did not give further details of Delage's condition or say when he might try to revive the project.
Delage planned the Ocean Observer project as both a personal challenge and a scientific mission to record marine life in the area and chart the effects of prolonged undersea isolation.
The craft is an underwater observatory supported by a steel float. It has no engine or sail and would be propelled only by sea currents and winds.
The French adventurer has a penchant for solo feats.

In 1991 he flew an ultra-light plane of his own design across the Atlantic in 26 hours and in December 1994 he embarked on an eight-week journey across the Atlantic, alternately swimming and floating on a raft.
That adventure was clouded in controversy over whether he was unduly helped by trade winds and sea currents and whether the journey had been a genuine feat or a publicity stunt.
